title: Your Next Off-Plan Project Is Sold by Your Last Building
seoTitle: Your Next Off-Plan Project Is Sold by Your Last Building
description: Off-plan buyers judge a new launch by the buildings a developer already delivered. How to show that track record before buyers go looking for it.
answer: Off-plan buyers no longer trust the story alone. They look up a developer's older projects, compare the old renderings with what stands today, and judge the new launch by that gap. So your next project is sold by your last building. Developers with a small gap should show that proof first, side by side, before buyers find it themselves.
body:
A new launch comes with new renderings, a new brochure and a new story. But the buyer sitting across the table is not thinking about your next building. They are thinking about your last one.

## Why your old projects matter more than your new renderings

The projects you launched five, seven or ten years ago are finished now. They are the only real evidence of what you deliver. A rendering shows what you hope to build. A finished building shows what you actually build. Buyers know the difference, and they act on it.

## What a buyer can find in one hour

They do not need a lawyer or an inspector. They need a phone and about an hour, and with AI tools the research is faster and deeper than ever. They find your old project on Google Maps, switch to Street View, and look at the facade, the landscaping, the finishing and the amenities. Then they search for the marketing you published back then, because those old renderings and videos are still online. They put the two side by side.

If the gap is big, the doubt does not stay with the old project. It moves straight to the one you are selling today.

## Turn your track record into proof

If your gap is small, you are sitting on the best marketing you will ever have, and most developers hide it on a portfolio page nobody reads. Do what your buyer is going to do anyway, before they do it:

1. Put your old renderings next to photos of the finished building.
2. Show the launch date and the delivery date.
3. List the amenities you promised and the amenities you delivered.

## Investigation or confidence

The same proof lands in two very different ways. When a buyer finds it alone, it feels like an investigation. When you show it first, it feels like confidence. In my experience, that difference shapes the whole conversation that follows.

Every building you deliver becomes evidence, for you or against you. Let your track record do the selling, not the narrative.

This point comes from a longer conversation. Listen to the full episode at [/podcast/off-plan-buyers-check-your-past-what-will-they-find/](/podcast/off-plan-buyers-check-your-past-what-will-they-find/).
takeaways: Buyers judge a new off-plan launch by the buildings the developer already delivered.
Old renderings stay online, so anyone can compare them with Street View in minutes.
A big gap on an old project creates doubt about the new one.
Developers with a small gap should publish the side-by-side proof themselves.
Proof a buyer finds alone feels like an investigation; proof you show first feels like confidence.
faq: Why do off-plan buyers look at a developer's old projects?
Finished projects are the only real evidence of what a developer delivers. Buyers compare the old marketing with the building that stands today to judge how reliable the new promise is.
How can a developer show their track record to buyers?
Place old renderings next to photos of the finished building, and show the launch date, the delivery date, and the amenities promised versus delivered.
Does AI make it easier to research a developer?
Yes. A buyer can already learn a lot in an hour on a phone, and AI tools make that research faster and deeper.
